sentences.text: This ancient creature was a slender fish made of cartilage that could reach forty centimeters in length.
Its skin was protected by a layer of tooth-like scales known as dermal denticles.
The front fins sat fourteen centimeters from the snout tip and stretched just over five centimeters along the body.
Each individual tooth carried between nine and seventeen pointed bumps depending on the specific species.
John E. Harris suggested the animal acted as a scavenger because its teeth were small.
However, Harris also noted that bony fish scales found in a stomach region imply a diet of other fish.
Scientists originally placed this animal in the family Coronodontidae, a group containing only two genera.
It lived during the Late Devonian Period.
Fossils of its teeth have been discovered in Utah, Nevada, Western Australia, and Russia.
Michał Ginter argued in 2008 that the teeth of Diademodus utahensis might have been weakly attached, restricting its ability to catch large prey.
